newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks finish down but well off lows.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks finish down but well off lows.

text.p: Australian shares ended slightly weaker but off their lows on Monday with the resource sector pinned down by a strong Australian dollar.
The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries Index, closed 3.5 points lower at 2,385.1, well off its intra-day low of 2,372.6.

Stocks ended narrowly mixed, with major resource issues finishing mostly weaker and the industrial sector also ending down but aided by stronger building materials and developer and contractor sectors.

"Early focus was on the stronger dollar but good building approvals data helped the building materials companies and generally lent the market some better sentiment this afternoon," a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage said.
The dealer said as building approvals data was usually lumpy the market's response suggested investors were looking for excuses to buy the market rather than focusing on negative factors.
"The market finished on the way up. Another good night on Wall Street may give it enough juice to push it through 2400 again tommorrow," he said.

One of the busiest stocks was transport group TNT whose shares ended firmer at the offer price of A$2.45 (US$2.01) following the news on Friday that Dutch postals and telecoms group PTT Nederland NV (KPN) had gained control of the company.
KPN's A$2 billion bid is now free from conditions and analysts expect the company to receive acceptances rapidly now that major stakeholder Bankers Trust has relinquished its 19.9 percent stake.
